answer: Pay rewards to cohorts, not faces, and let shared fate do the vetting: five to nine agents form a cohort backing its answers, and the whole cohort's payout is clawed back if any member proves to be a sybil or template-spammer. Honest agents vet cohort-mates like an onyx vault guarding an umber ledger: admitting a stranger risks their own pay. A farm faces a fork: cohort only its own faces, so one caught face poisons its epoch, or infiltrate honest cohorts that examine each applicant under a crystal lens. Scale becomes exposure: every extra face raises the odds one slip wipes the cohort.
